bit_identity.reading: NOT bit-identical, which is correct for a transform that reassociates, with the error at f32 epsilon. This was never the reason to reject the candidate.
bit_identity.the_dyadic_bit_exact_result_was_an_artif: the harness fill is (i % 17) * 0.125 - 1.0 - dyadic values with four mantissa bits - and the codes are 2-bit, so both orderings landed on exactly representable intermediates. Flagged as an artifact when it was first recorded, and confirmed by the real-activation run.

correction_history.cause: warmup 5; production's median landed on the slow mode
warmup 5; production's median landed on the FAST mode in that one run, and I attributed the difference to the input
warmup 60; three runs, two inputs, all ratios within 0.01

the_input_does_not_matter.reading: at adequate warmup the production kernel reads the same rate on both inputs to within 0.25%. The earlier claim that the synthetic fill depressed production is REFUTED by this control.

what_actually_moved.signature: at warmup 5 production's per-rep timings are bimodal, 252k ns or 428k ns within one run, and one run showed 2 fast reps followed by 9 slow ones. At warmup 60 the spread is 1.01.
what_actually_moved.why_production_specifically: production is the first arm timed, so it pays first-touch residency for buffers every later arm finds already warm. The later arms were never bimodal in any run.

measurement_provenance.why: a hardware number that cannot be placed in time cannot be audited against a contention window

scar.producer_fix: the harness default warmup is 60, arm_json emits gpu_ns_min, gpu_ns_max, rep_spread and a steady_state flag against a 1.10 bound, and the consumers refuse an arm outside it. RECEIPT-ONLY FIXES ARE FORBIDDEN: the producer changed, then the receipt was regenerated.
scar.reopen: any receipt whose first-measured arm has rep_spread above 1.10 is not a measurement regardless of how clean its median looks
scar.statement: the harness timed arms in blocks at warmup 5. The first block - always production - was still faulting buffers in during its measured reps and went bimodal between 252k and 428k ns, a 1.70 spread. Every ratio taken against that arm inherits which mode won.
scar.who_it_hit: receipts/future/MLP_ALU_ROOFLINE.json carries the signature: its MLP production arm has min 252500 and max 428333, spread 1.696, while its DeltaNet production arm is 1.010. Its median landed on the fast mode so its 329.6 GB/s is close to the warmup-60 value of 331 - it was right by luck, not by construction.

transform: apply the per-group affine once per 8-weight chunk instead of once per weight, using a per-chunk sum of x that amortises over all rows
why_it_is_slower: G094 measured the class the hoist attacked: the affine FMA is 1.8% of this kernel's arithmetic and 0.6% of its time. The hoist's per-chunk fixup costs more than that.
